title: Called up: family situation and brother's war work
summary: Unmarried, with his stepfather dead and his brother exempt as a welder building Liberty ships, he reported for the draft without dodging.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Okay. Well, so -- by gum, we're at the Army now.
(Laughter)
So what happened? You were called up.

Yeah. Well I decided, you know -- I said, "Well, my career has been interrupted, so what else is there?" You know. So I just -- I didn't try to dodge my obligations. I just went and said, "Here I am. Do whatever you want to do with me, but --,"
Were you married then, Kenny?
No.
No.
No. And my family only had -- I had one brother and his wife, that was my family.
What had happened to your stepfather, was he still alive?
No. He died, oh long, years before.
So he died. Did he never know you were making a success?
No, no. He died before I even really started, got into it.
What a shame. There a man was good and kind. It would be nice for him, wouldn't it.
That's right.
Yeah. I see, so there was your brother.
Yeah.
Did he get called up too?
No, he had a family and --
Yeah.
And he was an expert arc welder, so they put him on, making Liberty ships.
Oh.
So that was his --
Well, that was good, wasn't it?
Yeah. He was really an expert welder, so they kept him. Plus he had a family, and you know.
Yeah.
So --
Yeah. Well, so you got called up. Your stomach must have been in your boots, all the same.
Well --
I mean it's the unknown again, isn't it?
Yeah.
And not being master of your fate that's so hard.
Yeah, that's what -- well, what happened, after training -- I did my training in Camp Seibert, Alabama.
